reasoning: Every behaviour the plan rests on is observed or cited, each of the eight delta scenarios has a test that pins its whole outcome, the RED selection can be red, and the fresh-machine step now reaches the person through Install step 4.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1 rejects the two simpler channels (a tag Install bumps — #184: a project `ref` re-points no known marketplace, so it moves nothing; `main` — ships every merged PR before its release and the drift check compares releases, not commits); D2 states no release-please option moves a branch, so the added step is the minimum; D3 takes the standard Dependabot `ignore` over a bespoke check; D1 makes the machine step a printed `manual` row instead of `init` driving `claude`, which adds no code path. Scope is the four decisions #199 recorded; the drive-letter duplicates stay a non-goal with a follow-up issue.

map.evidence: Eight delta scenarios, eight map entries, every named test existing or written in Group 1: Channel render → test_plugin::test_marketplace_follows_stable + test_init_remote::test_installed_footprint_is_closed; Machine channel step → test_init_remote::test_manual_actions_are_printed (parametrized `--dry-run`/`--confirm`, test_init_remote.py:214, so both halves of its WHEN are covered); Release created → test_reusable_workflows::test_release_workflow_moves_stable, which pins both THEN clauses (the `if`/env/`force=false` and the absence of `continue-on-error`, `|| true`, `set +e`, so a refused update cannot pass silently); No release → the same test's `if` assertion; Dependabot render → test_init_config::test_dependabot_leaves_process_refs_to_install; Release recorded → test_config_block_records_release (unchanged); Release drift → test_start_change::test_release_drift, whose `_SKILL_FIX` constant pins the command and `--scope`; Publisher checkout → test_publisher_checkout_is_exempt (unchanged).

red.evidence: Group 1 writes three new tests (1.1, 1.2, 1.3) and edits five existing ones, and 1.5 names exactly the failing selection: the two parametrized ids `test_release_drift[newer-start_change]` / `[newer-create_tracking_issue]` (the only params `_SKILL_FIX` touches — the decorator order at test_start_change.py:730-731 puts `case` first in the id, matching the spelling used), the edited `test_rerender_replaces_only_owned_content`, both `test_manual_actions_are_printed` params, and `test_install_names_the_skill_marker`, which now also carries the `plugin-channel` assertion. Every named test fails in its body before implementation: no new production symbol appears, and each new assertion contradicts a value the current tree holds (`ref: v<version>`, no `autoUpdate`, no `plugin-channel` row, no `Move stable` step, no `ignore`, `/plugin marketplace update`), so `check_red.py`'s no-green rule (check_red.py:152) is satisfiable by this selection.

platform.evidence: Every behaviour the design rests on has an observation or a quoted reference. `claude plugin marketplace add "<repo>#stable"` re-points a known marketplace (#199 comment, step 3). User-scope `autoUpdate` moves the clone and the install records (proposal, positive control 2026-09-28 04:52:56Z→04:57:29Z), matching loading.md "When auto-update runs"; project-scope `autoUpdate` is no longer relied on — D1 replaces that reliance with the printed `manual plugin-channel` row carrying exactly the observed step-5 configuration. `claude plugin update agent-process@agent-process-marketplace --scope project --json` was observed to refresh the marketplace itself and update the install 2.0.0→2.6.0 (proposal 05:24Z: `known_marketplaces.json` `lastUpdated` 05:24:11.740Z immediately before the install record at 05:24:11.832Z), which closes the doubt that the documented refresh covers only `install`; `--scope <user|project>` and the scope `claude plugin list` prints are both real (`claude plugin update --help`: `-s, --scope <scope>` user/project/local/managed; `claude plugin list` prints `Scope: user` / `Scope: project` — both run on this machine, and the list also shows the drive-letter duplicates the Risks section describes). release-please-action emits `release_created`/`sha` unprefixed for the root `.` package (README "Root component outputs"; the manifest's only package is `.`), `force=false` makes the ref update a fast-forward or a refusal (docs.github.com "Update a reference"), and Dependabot `dependency-name` takes `*` (options reference).

replaced.evidence: D3 drops the only mechanism that pushed a new process release into a consumer repository (Dependabot's bump of `quality.yml@v<x.y.z>`) and lists beside the decision what is unknown (Dependabot's name form for a reusable-workflow dependency, hence the `*` wildcard) and what still holds (a half-update PR that appears anyway fails on `PR links no issue`); the #199 comment records that such a PR never proved release currency, and the replacement route — release drift plus re-running Install — is named. D1 likewise replaces a project-declared input (`autoUpdate` in the repository's settings) with a step the person performs, and names what no longer rests on it.

catcher.evidence: Four catchers, each traced to code or to a delivery step: a refused or failing `gh api` PATCH exits non-zero and fails the `Move stable to the release` step of the release-please run on the merge push (D2, pinned by 1.2's absence assertions); a consumer whose auto-updated skill outruns the recorded release is stopped by `init.release_drift` (init.py:344-364) in `create_tracking_issue`/`start_change`, exit 2 before any GitHub call, naming the scoped plugin-update fix; the drive-letter duplicates surface as `agent-process skill not loaded (several installs apply: …)` from the SessionStart hook (templates/skill_check.py:41-43); and the fresh-machine step now reaches the person through the step that relays the `manual` rows — 3.2 edits SKILL.md Install step 4 to name the `plugin-channel` row beside `project-*` and `review-secret`, and 1.4 pins `plugin-channel` in that step of `test_install_names_the_skill_marker` (whose `_section("Install")` text, test_planning_workflow.py:502, contains the numbered steps).

length.evidence: Spec sentences the plan adds or edits: the channel requirement's first sentence 24 words (both keys pinned in two renders and in the closed footprint); its new second sentence 44 words, pinned by the two `test_manual_actions_are_printed` params (exactly one `manual plugin-channel: ` row, the `marketplace add` command, `Enable auto-update`, no logged `claude` program) — every clause asserted, the last slightly narrower than the spec's "no command that changes plugin or marketplace state"; "a release moves the stable channel" 47 words, pinned clause by clause including the refusal; "Dependabot leaves process refs to Install" 18 words, pinned by list equality; the MODIFIED drift requirement grows by ~5 words ("with the install's scope"), pinned by `--scope` in `_SKILL_FIX` plus the `"#v"` absence. SKILL.md gains about ten words in Install step 4 (pinned by the `plugin-channel` assertion) and at most two sentences in the last paragraph (3.2 caps the migration at one, and three of its substrings are asserted); init.py gains one `_manual` row and one docstring line. The unpinned remainder is the migration sentence's wording.

bespoke.evidence: No new script and no new quality check. The only added mechanism is D2's workflow step, whose decision names the problem (#199), the standard (the reference's release-channel pattern, one ref per channel) and why nothing standard fits (no release-please option moves a branch; the existing tag-writing token, so no new secret). D1 keeps the machine step as a printed `manual` row rather than automation, D3 states the standard Dependabot `ignore` and rejects a bespoke check, and protecting `stable` is left to a repository ruleset the person adds.
